subject: Renewal & expansion pricing — volume step-ups, blended rates, new model routes
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novahealth.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@novahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Call recap + next steps (usage, target $/1M, expansion routes)

Hi Samantha / Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can align on pricing and renewal timing.

1) Current usage & ramp (from NovaHealth team): 300M tokens/mo (average), peaks up to ~480M in campaign weeks. You expect ~1.2B tokens/mo within 12 months if new routes roll out.

2) Budget & unit economics: you mentioned a target of ~$900 per 1M tokens as the budget target for long-term pricing. Important to confirm whether that target is aspirational or a firm internal benchmark for procurement.

3) Pricing levers we discussed: volume step-ups (tiered discounts as you scale), blended rates across model mix (production vs. cheaper quantized variants), and adding new routes/models (some routes can have lower-cost model choices).

4) Next steps I proposed on the call:
   - I’ll put together a draft tiered pricing worksheet showing step-ups and an illustrative blended rate based on your projected mix.
   - If procurement confirms a target $/1M, we’ll map to a renewal quote and draft SOW for signature.
   - Legal/procurement items: procurement timeline and any standard T&Cs/Procurement contact.

Attached: NovaHealth_Usage_2025Q4.csv (your usage export) — used for initial blended-rate calc.

Open questions for you: is the $900/1M a hard constraint? Do you expect the 1.2B ramp timing to be accelerated? Who (email) should we send the draft renewal/quote to for review?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a proposed price ladder by tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications:

- The 300M tokens/mo is current steady-state; the 1.2B is our internal plan with aggressive adoption — could be 9-12 months depending on pilot results.
- The $900/1M is a target from finance, not yet locked. Procurement will push for lower, but finance wants to see a blended/weighted example that gets us near that when volume scales and we introduce cheaper model routes.
- Please send the draft renewal + pricing to procurement@novahealth.com and cc me. Procurement wants the quote and SOW by the end of this month (target 2026-04-30).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-06T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing math for NovaHealth (draft tiers and blended calc)

Rishi / Monica — follow-up after Samantha’s note. Draft tiered ladder and sample blended-rate math below so we can move quickly on a formal quote. I’ll attach a cleaned spreadsheet for legal/procurement.

Assumptions:
- Current steady-state: 300M tokens/mo
- Forecasted ramp: 1.2B tokens/mo within 12 months
- Client target: ~$900 per 1M tokens (finance target)

Proposed step-ups (per 1M tokens):
- Tier A 0–100M: $1,200 / 1M
- Tier B 100–500M: $1,000 / 1M
- Tier C 500–1500M: $800 / 1M

Illustrative blended rate (current 300M):
- 100M at $1,200 = $120,000
- 200M at $1,000 = $200,000
- Total cost = $320,000 for 300M -> blended = $1,066.67 per 1M tokens

Illustrative blended rate (projected 1.2B):
- 100M @ $1,200 = $120,000
- 400M @ $1,000 = $400,000
- 700M @ $800 = $560,000
- Total = $1,080,000 for 1,200M -> blended = $900 per 1M tokens (hits their target)

Notes / levers to get lower:
- Adding a low-cost quantized route for high-volume batch jobs (e.g., $600 / 1M) for non-latency-critical requests; if 30% of volume moves, blended improves materially.
- Prefix/KV cache and intelligent batching can reduce billable tokens for repeated prompts; we can model savings separately.
- Commitment/term: 12–24 month volume commitments can lower step prices another ~10–15% depending on guarantee.

Questions: are we comfortable positioning the Tier C $800 /1M level as achievable with a 1.0B+ commitment? I'd like to include legal/finance note on minimum committed volume for those discounts. Also should we propose a blended rate guarantee for the renewal term (e.g., target blended $/1M capped if they hit volume bands)?

I’ll draft the pricing spreadsheet and a short summary to send to procurement@novahealth.com.

—Marissa

From: Tom Harris <tharris@novahealth.com>

Thanks Marissa — the tiered ladder looks good. A couple of asks from our side before procurement will sign off:

- Can you provide a worked example showing a 70/30 model mix (70% production high-quality model, 30% cheaper quantized model) and the resulting blended $/1M at both 300M and 1.2B volumes?
- Procurement will want a formal renewal quote and SOW (DocuSign). We need to see SLA details for latency and uptime for the Dedicated pool if we go that route.

Samantha: procurement@novahealth.com is looped. We’re aiming to have the quote reviewed by legal next week.

—Tom
VP, Platform Engineering
Nova Health

Subject: Proposed pricing spreadsheet + next steps (attached)

Hi Samantha / Tom / Procurement — attaching the pricing workbook (Proposed_Pricing_2026_v3.xlsx) and a short summary below:

1) Worked examples included in the sheet:
   - 70/30 model mix example (70% production @ Tier rates, 30% quantized @ $600 /1M).
   - Blended results: 300M -> blended ~$940 /1M (with 70/30 mix); 1.2B -> blended ~$760 /1M (with 70/30 mix and Tier C allocation).
2) Proposed step-ups (as shared): Tier A $1,200; Tier B $1,000; Tier C $800. Quantized route set at $600 /1M for batch jobs.
3) Commitment options: 12-month (baseline discount), 24-month (additional 10% off step prices), and usage true-up quarterly.
4) SLA summary (Dedicated): 99.9% uptime SLA, P75 latency targets per model in the sheet; full SLA/terms to be included in SOW.

Next steps:
- We’ll prepare a draft renewal/quote + SOW and send via DocuSign to procurement@novahealth.com by 2026-04-15 for legal review.
- Please confirm if procurement needs any specific PO/contract language attached; we’ll loop legal.
- If procurement wants a PoC to validate blended costs, we can arrange a 30–60 day pilot with trial credits to validate token counts and model-mix savings.

Attached files: Proposed_Pricing_2026_v3.xlsx
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890 (tracked).

Thanks — will follow-up with DocuSign draft later this week.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the detail. Two quick items before we finalize:

1) Procurement asked if Redwood can provide a small trial credit to validate the blended-rate assumptions (30–60 days, up to ~50M billable tokens). That will help mitigate procurement risk.
2) Can you confirm the Dedicated SLA is applicable to the Tier C pricing bands if we commit to the volume? Procurement will want that in writing.

If you can confirm both, we’ll prioritize legal review and aim to return a signed SOW within two weeks.

—Tom
